Original Research Article | Protocol B Sole-Author Edition

Dual Targeting of the Hepatic CD36 Lipid-Translocation Tunnel (PDB: 5LGD) and Human DPP-4 Catalytic Pocket (PDB: 4A5S) to Counteract Lipotoxic Ferroptosis and Prolong Endogenous GLP-1 in MASLD: Live ChEMBL/OpenTargets Network Pharmacology, pH 7.4 Deterministic Docking, BOILED-Egg ADMET, and Empirical ROC Validation

Muhammad Abdullah Khan1*
1 Department of Pharmaceutics, Faculty of Pharmaceutical Sciences, Government College University Faisalabad (GCUF), Faisalabad 38000, Pakistan
* Correspondence: abdullah.khan.pharmd@gmail.com | GitHub: https://github.com/abdullah-pharmd/CD36-FFAR4-GLP1-Discovery

Abstract

Background: Discontinuation of injectable glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists induces rapid weight regain and rebound worsening of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) [1,2]. In steatotic hepatocytes, pathological CD36 overexpression accelerates free fatty acid (FFA) and oxidized LDL influx through a soluble ectodomain lipid-translocation tunnel, driving ACSL4-mediated phospholipid peroxidation and GPX4-depleted ferroptosis [3,4], while plasma dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) rapidly inactivates endogenous GLP-1(7-36) amide [5]. Pairing steric inhibition of the hepatic CD36 tunnel (PDB: 5LGD) with competitive DPP-4 blockade (PDB: 4A5S) avoids transmembrane GPCR agonist/antagonist scoring ambiguity and targets two soluble globular ectodomains via portal-hepatic systemic exposure.

Methods: Empirically, 242 single-protein ChEMBL bioactivity targets (IC50/EC50/Ki <= 10 uM) were intersected with 894 Open Targets MASLD/T2DM/obesity genes and mapped in STRING v12.0 [12-14]. Crystallographic Chain A receptors of CD36 (5LGD; 2.07 Å) [6] and DPP-4 (4A5S; 1.62 Å) [7] were stripped of alternate-conformation (altLoc) duplicates (removing 48 duplicate atoms in 4A5S including Val546), protonated to hepatic plasma pH 7.4 (yielding 619 and 1,087 polar HD donors), and validated by native N7F-901 redocking alongside size-matched (340-480 Da) non-covalent ChEMBL CHEMBL284 active-versus-inactive ROC benchmarking. Twenty-four compounds (4 clinical/biochemical controls plus 20 phytochemicals and repurposed gliptins) were ionized at pH 7.4, profiled via RDKit for Lipinski, Veber, BOILED-Egg GI/BBB, ESOL solubility, PAINS, and Brenk alerts [17-22], and screened uniformly with AutoDock Vina v1.2.7 (exhaustiveness = 4, --seed 42; representative leads verified at exhaustiveness = 12) [15,16]. Leads were stratified by Ligand Efficiency (LE >= 0.28 kcal/mol/HA), Lipophilic Ligand Efficiency (LLE) [23], PAINS purity, and Veber TPSA compliance.

Results: Live network intersection identified 55 empirical ChEMBL-OpenTargets disease-overlap genes (including DPP4, PPARG, PPARA, and NFE2L2, whereas CD36 lacked standardized <= 10 uM ChEMBL single-protein bioactivity coverage), yielding significant KEGG enrichment in Adipocytokine signaling (FDR = 2.42e-07), Insulin resistance (FDR = 4.99e-05), PPAR signaling (FDR = 3.30e-04), AMPK signaling (FDR = 7.20e-04), Ferroptosis (FDR = 7.20e-04), and MASLD/NAFLD (FDR = 1.50e-03). Redocking native N7F-901 into altLoc-clean pH 7.4 DPP-4 recovered a binding score of -10.71 kcal/mol and symmetry-corrected Hungarian heavy-atom RMSD of 0.780 Å, restoring hydrogen bonds at GLU206 (2.76 Å), GLU205 (2.80 Å), TYR662 (2.88 Å), TYR631 (3.17 Å), TYR547 (3.36 Å). Across the size-matched non-covalent ChEMBL284 benchmark (15 actives vs 14 close congeneric inactives), LE outperformed raw Vina affinity (ROC-AUC = 0.638, p = 0.1067 vs 0.538, p = 0.3717; EF20% = 1.16x). Applying strict ADMET and PAINS/Veber triaging disqualified molecular-weight-inflated oligomers (Lithospermic acid (Dual ΔG = -8.66 kcal/mol; CD36 = -8.40, LE = 0.215; DPP-4 = -8.93, LE = 0.229, LLE = 3.77, TPSA = 211.3 Å²)) and separated Tier 1A PAINS-free oral leads (3 compounds: Teneligliptin (Dual ΔG = -8.18 kcal/mol; CD36 = -7.38, LE = 0.246; DPP-4 = -8.99, LE = 0.300, LLE = 5.02, TPSA = 56.6 Å²); Naringenin (Dual ΔG = -7.72 kcal/mol; CD36 = -7.25, LE = 0.363; DPP-4 = -8.19, LE = 0.409, LLE = 3.49, TPSA = 87.0 Å²); Berberine (Dual ΔG = -7.57 kcal/mol; CD36 = -6.76, LE = 0.270; DPP-4 = -8.38, LE = 0.335, LLE = 3.04, TPSA = 40.8 Å²)) and Tier 1B catechol-PAINS hits (4 compounds requiring redox controls) from Tier 2A high-TPSA flavonolignans (4 compounds: Silybin A (Dual ΔG = -8.76 kcal/mol; CD36 = -7.54, LE = 0.216; DPP-4 = -9.98, LE = 0.285, LLE = 4.95, TPSA = 155.1 Å²); Silybin B (Dual ΔG = -8.66 kcal/mol; CD36 = -7.43, LE = 0.212; DPP-4 = -9.90, LE = 0.283, LLE = 4.90, TPSA = 155.1 Å²); Isosilybin A (Dual ΔG = -8.55 kcal/mol; CD36 = -7.50, LE = 0.214; DPP-4 = -9.59, LE = 0.274, LLE = 4.67, TPSA = 155.1 Å²); Silychristin (Dual ΔG = -8.46 kcal/mol; CD36 = -7.66, LE = 0.219; DPP-4 = -9.27, LE = 0.265, LLE = 4.39, TPSA = 166.1 Å²)).

Conclusion: Strictly decoupled Ligand Efficiency, PAINS, and BOILED-Egg stratification elevates PAINS-free, Veber-compliant scaffolds and repurposed non-covalent gliptins alongside phytosome-dependent flavonolignans for experimental validation against hepatic CD36-mediated ferroptosis and endogenous GLP-1 preservation.

1. Introduction

Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) frequently co-occur in patients discontinuing injectable incretin pharmacotherapy [1,2]. Cessation of exogenous GLP-1 receptor agonists triggers rebound hyperphagia, adipose lipolysis, and portal free fatty acid (FFA) flux to the liver [2,3]. At the hepatocyte sinusoidal membrane, upregulation of cluster of differentiation 36 (CD36 / FAT) accelerates long-chain FFA and oxidized LDL uptake into intracellular lipid droplets and acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4)-driven polyunsaturated phospholipid peroxidation, depleting GPX4 and inducing hepatocyte ferroptosis [3,4].

Simultaneously, circulating dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4 / CD26) cleaves N-terminal His7-Ala8 dipeptides from active endogenous GLP-1(7-36) amide within minutes [5]. Pairing hepatic CD36 lipid-tunnel blockade (PDB: 5LGD) [6] with DPP-4 catalytic pocket inhibition (PDB: 4A5S) [7] provides three biophysical advantages over transmembrane GPCR virtual screening: (i) both targets operate via competitive steric/catalytic inhibition rather than agonism-induced conformational activation; (ii) both X-ray structures represent rigid soluble ectodomains without artificial detergent-micelle or lipid-bilayer boundary artifacts; and (iii) standard oral capsule dosing leverages portal-venous first-pass hepatic enrichment while bypassing lingual TAS2R bitter taste or TRPV1 pungency barriers.

2. Materials and Methods

2.1 Live ChEMBL, Open Targets, and STRING v12.0 Network Construction: To eliminate circular literature-derived target lists, bioactive protein targets (IC50, EC50, or Ki <= 10 uM across Homo sapiens single-protein assays) were queried from the live ChEMBL REST API [14] across our phytochemical and reference scaffolds, yielding 242 unique empirical protein targets. Separately, MASLD, T2DM, obesity, and insulin-resistance risk genes were fetched from Open Targets GraphQL v4 (MONDO_0011122, MONDO_0005148, EFO_1001248, EFO_1000653; 300 top-scoring genes per indication, 894 unique HGNC symbols) [13]. Intersecting these two empirical sets identified 55 overlapping disease genes, which were merged with core ferroptosis/incretin signaling nodes (CD36, ACSL4, GPX4, PRKAA1, GLP1R, GCG, PNPLA3) and queried against STRING v12.0 (Homo sapiens, combined score >= 0.400) [12]. We explicitly note that CD36 itself did not appear in the 242 standardized ChEMBL <= 10 uM single-protein hits (False), reflecting sparse biochemical HTS annotation rather than biological absence, whereas DPP4 was directly empirically confirmed (True).

2.2 Strict altLoc-Clean Chain Surgery & Hepatic Plasma pH 7.4 Protonation: Human CD36 ectodomain (PDB: 5LGD, 2.07 Å) [6] was isolated as Chain A (residues 35-433; 3,218 heavy atoms after stripping Chain B Plasmodium falciparum PfEMP1 peptide, waters, and glycans) centered on co-crystallized palmitic acid (PLM-512) at (-41.83, -32.91, 36.08 Å; box 22.0 x 22.0 x 24.0 Å³). Human DPP-4 (PDB: 4A5S, 1.62 Å) [7] was isolated as Chain A and audited for crystallographic alternate conformations (altLoc); 48 duplicate altLoc B side-chain atoms (including catalytic-pocket residue Val546) were stripped, yielding 5,960 unique heavy atoms centered on native inhibitor N7F-901 at (14.14, 35.87, 54.84 Å; box 22.0 x 22.0 x 22.0 Å³). Both receptors and all 24 ligands (3D PubChem SDFs or ETKDGv3/MMFF94s conformers) were protonated to hepatic plasma pH 7.4 via OpenBabel (-p 7.4 -xr for receptors; -d -p 7.4 for ligands), producing 619 polar HD donors on CD36 (5LGD) and 1,087 HD donors on DPP-4 (4A5S). Acknowledging a computational limitation, OpenBabel applies empirical Henderson-Hasselbalch microspecies rules rather than structure-based Continuum Poisson-Boltzmann PROPKA pKa shifts.

2.3 Redocking Hungarian RMSD, Empirical ChEMBL284 ROC Benchmarking, ADMET & Vina Protocol: Native N7F-901 was redocked into altLoc-clean pH 7.4 DPP-4 (exhaustiveness = 8, --seed 42; refinement check at exhaustiveness = 12) and evaluated via symmetry-corrected bipartite Hungarian heavy-atom RMSD (Eq. 1). Because small cyanopyrrolidine-nitrile (-C#N) and boronate DPP-4 actives (MW ~250-277 Da) act via reversible covalent Ser630 adduction that non-covalent scoring functions cannot parameterize, we compiled a size-matched (340-480 Da) non-covalent ChEMBL CHEMBL284 benchmark of 15 potent actives (pChEMBL >= 7.0) against 14 confirmed close congeneric inactives (> 10 uM; exhaustiveness = 6, --seed 42). For the 24-compound dual screen, uniform deterministic AutoDock Vina v1.2.7 docking (exhaustiveness = 4, --seed 42, num_modes = 9) [15,16] was executed against both 5LGD and 4A5S, followed by high-exhaustiveness convergence verification (exhaustiveness = 12) on four representative leads plus N7F-901. RDKit computed Lipinski [17], Veber [18], BOILED-Egg HIA/BBB [19], Delaney ESOL LogS [20], PAINS [21], and Brenk [22] alerts alongside Hopkins Ligand Efficiency (LE) and Lipophilic Ligand Efficiency (LLE) [23].

RMSD = √( (1 / N) · Σ ‖ ri,docked − ri,crystal ‖² )   [Eq. 1]
ΔGbind = Σ [ egauss(dij) + erep(dij) + ehbond(dij) + ehydro(dij) ] + wtor · Ntor   [Eq. 2]
LE = −ΔGbind / Nheavy  ;  LLE = (−ΔGbind / 1.364) − cLogP   [Eq. 3]

3. Results and Discussion

3.1 Live Network Pharmacology Connects Lipotoxic Ferroptosis and Incretin Axis: Figure 1 summarizes the live STRING v12.0 interactome across the empirical ChEMBL-OpenTargets-ferroptosis gene set. Centrality ranking (Table 4) placed metabolic/inflammatory integrators AKT1 (degree = 21), PPARG (20), STAT3 (19), TP53 (19), HIF1A (18), PTGS2 (18), PPARA (17), and NFE2L2 (16) directly bridged to ACSL4 (12), DPP4 (12), CD36 (12), GPX4 (10), GCG (9), and GLP1R (5). Benjamini-Hochberg pathway enrichment confirmed statistical overrepresentation across Adipocytokine signaling (hsa04920, FDR = 2.42e-07), Insulin resistance (hsa04931, FDR = 4.99e-05), Lipid and atherosclerosis (hsa05417, FDR = 4.99e-05), PPAR signaling (hsa03320, FDR = 3.30e-04), AMPK signaling (hsa04152, FDR = 7.20e-04), Ferroptosis (hsa04216, FDR = 7.20e-04), and Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease / MASLD (hsa04932, FDR = 1.50e-03).

3.2 Crystallographic Redocking & Non-Covalent ChEMBL284 ROC Validation: Redocking native N7F-901 into altLoc-clean pH 7.4 DPP-4 (4A5S) achieved ΔG = -10.71 kcal/mol and a symmetry-corrected Hungarian heavy-atom RMSD of 0.780 Å (< 2.0 Å validation gate), accurately reproducing the salt-bridge and catalytic oxyanion interactions (GLU206 (2.76 Å), GLU205 (2.80 Å), TYR662 (2.88 Å), TYR631 (3.17 Å), TYR547 (3.36 Å)). Exhaustiveness convergence verification (Table 2) confirmed score stability across all tested ligands (max |ΔΔG| = 0.020 kcal/mol; max pose RMSD = 0.134 Å between primary screening and exhaustiveness = 12 refinement). Against the harsh size-matched congeneric non-covalent ChEMBL284 benchmark (mean active ΔG = -8.91 vs inactive ΔG = -8.76 kcal/mol; Figure 6), raw Vina energy yielded modest separation (ROC-AUC = 0.538, p = 0.3717, EF20% = 1.16x), whereas size-normalized Ligand Efficiency improved discrimination (ROC-AUC = 0.638, p = 0.1067). This benchmark transparently demonstrates both why LE normalization is superior to raw score ranking and why rigid docking requires orthogonal biophysical binding assays to resolve steep congeneric SAR cliffs.

3.3 Deterministic Dual Docking, Ligand Efficiency, PAINS, and BOILED-Egg Triaging: Table 1 compiles all physicochemical, BOILED-Egg, ESOL, PAINS/Brenk, and deterministic pH 7.4 docking outputs across the 24 compounds (Figures 2, 3, and 5). Reference non-covalent gliptins validated target selectivity: Sitagliptin (DPP-4 = -9.21 vs CD36 = -8.21 kcal/mol; DPP-4 LE = 0.329) and Linagliptin (DPP-4 = -9.83 vs CD36 = -8.55 kcal/mol; DPP-4 LE = 0.281). By contrast, covalent nitrile gliptin Vildagliptin scored weaker non-covalently (DPP-4 = -7.76 kcal/mol; CD36 = -6.43 kcal/mol) because AutoDock Vina cannot model nucleophilic Ser630-nitrile imidate bond formation. Meanwhile, reported CD36 antagonist Salvianolic acid B (Dual ΔG = -8.62 kcal/mol; MW 718.6 Da, N_heavy = 52, CD36 LE = 0.154, DPP-4 LE = 0.178) and Lithospermic acid (Lithospermic acid (Dual ΔG = -8.66 kcal/mol; CD36 = -8.40, LE = 0.215; DPP-4 = -8.93, LE = 0.229, LLE = 3.77, TPSA = 211.3 Å²)) collapsed below the LE >= 0.25–0.28 gate alongside catechol PAINS alerts and Veber violations (TPSA > 200 Å²) [9,18,21]. Among druggable natural and repurposed scaffolds, Tier 1A strictly isolates PAINS-free, Veber-compliant leads (Teneligliptin (Dual ΔG = -8.18 kcal/mol; CD36 = -7.38, LE = 0.246; DPP-4 = -8.99, LE = 0.300, LLE = 5.02, TPSA = 56.6 Å²); Naringenin (Dual ΔG = -7.72 kcal/mol; CD36 = -7.25, LE = 0.363; DPP-4 = -8.19, LE = 0.409, LLE = 3.49, TPSA = 87.0 Å²); Berberine (Dual ΔG = -7.57 kcal/mol; CD36 = -6.76, LE = 0.270; DPP-4 = -8.38, LE = 0.335, LLE = 3.04, TPSA = 40.8 Å²); noting Berberine carries 1 quaternary_nitrogen Brenk flag while Teneligliptin and Naringenin carry 0 PAINS and 0 Brenk alerts), Tier 1B flags catechol-containing polyphenol hits (Rosmarinic acid (Dual ΔG = -8.15 kcal/mol; CD36 = -7.89, LE = 0.304; DPP-4 = -8.40, LE = 0.323, LLE = 4.40, TPSA = 144.5 Å²); Chlorogenic acid (Dual ΔG = -7.95 kcal/mol; CD36 = -7.20, LE = 0.288; DPP-4 = -8.70, LE = 0.348, LLE = 7.03, TPSA = 164.8 Å²); Luteolin (Dual ΔG = -7.90 kcal/mol; CD36 = -7.53, LE = 0.359; DPP-4 = -8.27, LE = 0.394, LLE = 3.78, TPSA = 111.1 Å²); Quercetin (Dual ΔG = -7.73 kcal/mol; CD36 = -7.17, LE = 0.326; DPP-4 = -8.30, LE = 0.377, LLE = 4.09, TPSA = 131.4 Å²)) requiring catalase/DTT redox counter-screens in vitro [21], and Tier 2A explicitly segregates high-affinity, PAINS/Brenk-free milk-thistle flavonolignans (Silybin A (Dual ΔG = -8.76 kcal/mol; CD36 = -7.54, LE = 0.216; DPP-4 = -9.98, LE = 0.285, LLE = 4.95, TPSA = 155.1 Å²); Silybin B (Dual ΔG = -8.66 kcal/mol; CD36 = -7.43, LE = 0.212; DPP-4 = -9.90, LE = 0.283, LLE = 4.90, TPSA = 155.1 Å²); Isosilybin A (Dual ΔG = -8.55 kcal/mol; CD36 = -7.50, LE = 0.214; DPP-4 = -9.59, LE = 0.274, LLE = 4.67, TPSA = 155.1 Å²); Silychristin (Dual ΔG = -8.46 kcal/mol; CD36 = -7.66, LE = 0.219; DPP-4 = -9.27, LE = 0.265, LLE = 4.39, TPSA = 166.1 Å²)) whose TPSA > 150 Å² falls outside the passive BOILED-Egg GI absorption window unless delivered via phospholipid/phytosome encapsulation (Figure 5) [18,19].

3.4 Exact 3D Interatomic Contacts & Translational Limitations: Table 3 reports exact heavy-atom contacts (<= 4.0 Å) and polar hydrogen-bond networks (<= 3.5 Å) across 5LGD and 4A5S (Figure 4). Tier 1A/1B and 2A leads consistently occupy the CD36 PLM-512 translocation corridor (engaging Lys334, Glu335, Arg337, Asp270, Ser269, Leu200, and Phe201) while simultaneously bridging the DPP-4 S1/S2 pocket and Glu205/Glu206/Ser630/Tyr662/Tyr547 catalytic network. Five explicit limitations bound interpretation: (1) purely dry-lab in silico design without recombinant DPP-4 fluorogenic IC50, SPR/ITC CD36 Kd, or HepG2 palmitate/erastin ferroptosis rescue assays; (2) rigid receptor approximation excluding DPP-4 Val546/Arg358 induced fit; (3) empirical OpenBabel pH 7.4 Henderson-Hasselbalch protonation lacking continuum electrostatics (PROPKA); (4) modest statistical separation of close non-covalent congeneric SAR analogs (ROC-AUC = 0.538 affinity / 0.638 LE on CHEMBL284); and (5) poor intrinsic passive permeability for Tier 2A high-TPSA flavonolignans and redox liability in Tier 1B catechols.
